summary: Sticky captive portal sessions keep devices on guest VLAN, causing split-tunnel VPN traffic failures
description:
Issue summary: Several employees report intermittent failures when their MacBooks (macOS 13/14) connect to the corporate wifi after being offsite or using a hotspot. Affected devices appear to remain on the guest VLAN with a captive-portal binding even after successful SSO authentication, so split-tunnel VPN traffic to internal services is routed incorrectly and is blocked by firewall rules.

Impact: ~12 users in the SF office and some remote users experienced loss of access to internal services (internal API, dev dashboards) while appearing connected to wifi and VPN. Productivity impact for those users is high; they must use mobile hotspot or wired connection to restore full access.

Environment: Production corporate SSID (corp-ssid) with per-user auth and split-tunnel VPN policy. Wireless controller version 8.2.3, AP firmware 5.14, firewall NAT and conntrack on edge appliances. Mac clients (macOS 13/14) and a handful of Linux laptops observed.

Observed behavior: After SSO success users still get an HTTP redirect to captive portal for some internal addresses; VPN establishes but internal traffic is NAT'd on guest VLAN and firewall denies it. Wireless controller console shows a persistent captive-session mapping tied to client MAC that is not cleared by reauth or DHCP renew.

Expected behavior: Successful auth moves client to corporate VLAN, split-tunnel routes internal destinations over the corporate path and the VPN tunnel as expected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Join corp-ssid from macOS 14 client that was previously connected to guest or a different AP.
2) Authenticate via SSO captive portal when prompted (Microsoft SSO).
3) Observe client receives corporate VLAN IP and attempts to start split-tunnel VPN (WireGuard).
4) Attempt to access internal API (https://internal.api.redwood/) — client is redirected to captive portal instead of receiving a 200, and packets show NAT via guest VLAN.
5) Check wireless controller: captive session entry remains bound to MAC and AP, even after reauth, DHCP renew, and client roaming.

Mar 10 09:14:43 Firewall: DROP tcp src=10.223.45.12:52344 dst=10.10.5.8:443 reason=zone-mismatch

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed pattern across multiple users, reproduced on macOS 13 and 14 with vendor APs in SF office.

Wireless team (Lucas Ortega): Controller shows captive-session sticky flag set; controller config has 'sticky-client' enabled for faster roaming. Suspect sticky assignment kept client on guest VLAN when AP switched contexts.
SRE (Priya Rao): Conntrack entries on the firewall showed NAT mapping to guest-zone IPs. Long conntrack timeouts (~600s) mean stale NAT mappings persist after VLAN move.

Hypothesis: Combination of controller's sticky-client + aggressive AP band-steering + long conntrack NAT timeouts leads to clients being authenticated but their IP/MAC binding still associated with guest-zone NAT path, causing split-tunnel traffic to be misrouted/blocked.

Packet captures: Showed SYNs from client going out with guest-zone source IP and firewall dropping because policy expects corporate subnet. AP logs indicate an incomplete VLAN reassignment event followed by auth success.
Reproduce notes: Forcing DHCP release on client occasionally clears the state; disabling sticky-client on a test AP prevented the issue during a 4-hour window.
Temporary mitigation attempted: Reduced conntrack timeout for established TCP from 600s to 120s on edge firewall (quick test) — some clients recovered after timeout expiry; not ideal for long-term.
Controller vendor advised there is a known edge-case with sticky-client and captive portal handoff in firmware <=5.14; recommended firmware 5.16+ where captive mappings are cleared on VLAN change.
User impact estimate: ~0.5% of daily connections based on AP session logs over last 48 hours, concentrated in SF and some remote clients using hotspot-to-wifi handover.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:30 - Maya Patel (Support): Ticket created after 3 reports arrived in #internal-support. Collected initial logs and asked for wireless controller debug output.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Lucas Ortega (Wireless): Confirmed sticky-client is enabled globally. I can repro on AP-12 in SF lab. Will test disabling sticky on one AP and watch for failures.

2026-03-10 11:22 - Priya Rao (SRE): Observed conntrack entries mapping corporate clients to guest NAT 10.33.5.x. Lowering conntrack timeout temporarily to 120s caused a couple of clients to recover; this supports NAT state persistence hypothesis.

2026-03-10 13:10 - Vendor Support (Aruba/Tx): Reported a firmware issue where captive portal session state isn't cleared on VLAN reassign with sticky-client enabled (FW <=5.14). Recommended upgrade to 5.16 and a controller config option to 'clear-captive-on-vlan-change'.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Evan Chen (NetOps): Applied sticky-client=false to AP-12 and AP-14 as a controlled test. No new incidents on those APs in the next 6 hours. Planning to roll config change to affected floors.

2026-03-11 16:45 - Lucas Ortega (Wireless): Scheduled rolling AP firmware upgrade to 5.16 next week with maintenance window and staged rollback plan. Will also enable 'clear-captive-on-vlan-change' if available.

2026-03-12 08:10 - Maya Patel (Support): Workarounds communicated to users: 1) Disable and re-enable Wi‑Fi to force DHCP/rebind, 2) Use wired connection, 3) Use mobile hotspot until controller patch is applied. Adding KB link.

2026-03-12 12:30 - Evan Chen (NetOps): Pushed controller config change to disable sticky-client on first-floor AP group and reduced conntrack timeout to 180s cluster-wide. Monitoring dashboards for errors and auth churn.
resolution: Workaround applied: disabled sticky-client on affected AP groups and reduced firewall conntrack timeout to 180s to reduce impact while vendor firmware upgrade is scheduled. Long-term fix: staged AP firmware upgrade to 5.16 and enable controller option to clear captive-session on VLAN change. Follow-up action: verify rollout during maintenance window and monitor session churn metrics for 72 hours.
